name: sa_0001
text:
The drawing shows N-fluorobenzenesulfonimide (NFSI). A central nitrogen carries one fluorine and is bonded to two sulfur atoms. Each sulfur has two double-bonded oxygens (a sulfonyl group) and one phenyl group, labelled "Ph" in the image, which I expanded to c1ccccc1.

SMILES: O=S(=O)(c1ccccc1)N(F)S(=O)(=O)c1ccccc1

name: sa_0003
text:
The drawing shows MeO2C–C≡C–CO2Me, which is dimethyl acetylenedicarboxylate.

- Each end is a methyl ester, MeO2C, written as C(=O)OC.
- The center is a carbon–carbon triple bond joining the two ester carbons.

The SMILES is COC(=O)C#CC(=O)OC. It is valid and matches the drawing atom for atom, and no stereochemistry is shown.

SMILES: COC(=O)C#CC(=O)OC

name: sa_0002
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with four substituents:

- A dipropylamino group, N(nPr)2, on the ring carbon at the right.
- A nitro group on each of the two ring carbons next to it (top and bottom).
- A CF3 group on the ring carbon opposite the amine (left).

This is trifluralin, which is N,N-dipropyl-2,6-dinitro-4-(trifluoromethyl)aniline. Each nPr is written as CCC.

SMILES: CCCN(CCC)c1c([N+](=O)[O-])cc(C(F)(F)F)cc1[N+](=O)[O-]

name: sa_0005
text:
The drawing shows diethyl azodicarboxylate (DEAD): an N=N double bond with an EtO2C group on each nitrogen.

Stereochemistry: the drawing shows the N=N bond in a zigzag layout, with the left carbon above the N–N axis and the right carbon below it, which looks trans (E). The bond lines are plain, with no explicit wedges or hashes, but the geometry is drawn as trans, so I include the E double-bond stereo.

Checking the geometry: the left N is at upper left, with its substituent C further to the lower left. The right N is at lower right, with its substituent C to the upper right. The N=N bond runs from upper left to lower right. Relative to that bond, the left substituent sits on the lower-left side and the right substituent on the upper-right side, so they are on opposite sides, which is trans.

SMILES for the E isomer: CCOC(=O)/N=N/C(=O)OCC

SMILES: CCOC(=O)/N=N/C(=O)OCC

name: sa_0004
text:
The drawing shows Boc-protected tyrosine with a benzyl ether on the phenol oxygen (Boc-Tyr(Bn)-OH).

- **Backbone:** the alpha carbon carries an NH–Boc group, a CO2H group and a CH2 group leading to a para-substituted benzene ring. The ring carries OBn (O–CH2–C6H5) opposite the CH2.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CO2H bond is drawn as a wedge, so it points toward the viewer and the implicit H points away. Viewed from the front, N (up) → CO2H (lower left) → CH2 (lower right) runs counterclockwise. With H at the back, that gives S, the L-amino-acid configuration.
- **SMILES form:** the fragment N[C@@H](CR)C(=O)O encodes L-tyrosine, so I used the same pattern here.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N[C@@H](Cc1ccc(OCc2ccccc2)cc1)C(=O)O

name: sa_0007
text:
This is osimertinib mesylate: the osimertinib free base drawn together with methanesulfonic acid as a separate component.

**Osimertinib part**
- Central benzene ring: a C(=O)C=C acrylamide on NH, a N(C)CCN(C)C group, an OMe, and an NH linking to the pyrimidine.
- Pyrimidine: its 4-position carries the 1-methylindol-3-yl group, and its 2-position carries the NH.
- Substituent order around the benzene ring, starting from the NH-acrylamide carbon: C1 bears NHC(=O)C=C, C2 bears N(C)CCN(C)C (at the top), C3 is CH, C4 bears OMe, C5 bears the NH to the pyrimidine, and C6 is CH.

**SMILES for the free base**
C=CC(=O)Nc1cc(Nc2nccc(n2)-c2cn(C)c3ccccc23)c(OC)cc1N(C)CCN(C)C

**Mesylate**
The acid is written as CS(=O)(=O)O, joined to the base with a dot.

SMILES: C=CC(=O)Nc1cc(Nc2nccc(n2)-c2cn(C)c3ccccc23)c(OC)cc1N(C)CCN(C)C.CS(=O)(=O)O

name: sa_0010
text:
This is Danishefsky's diene: 1-methoxy-3-trimethylsilyloxy-1,3-butadiene.

Reading the drawing, atoms run left to right:
- MeO at the left, bonded to C1 at about (512, 715).
- C1=C2, where C2 is at about (718, 880).
- C2–C3, where C3 is at about (965, 780).
- C3=CH2, with the CH2 at the top (about (980, 520)).
- C3–OTMS, with the OTMS at the lower right.

**Stereochemistry:** The C1=C2 double bond has OMe on C1 and the C3 chain on C2. The OMe goes from C1 down-left to O at (310, 795), and the C3 chain goes from C2 up-right. The two substituents point to opposite sides of the double bond, so the geometry is trans (E).

In SMILES, written as CO/C=C/C(=C)O[Si](C)(C)C, the "/" marks place the OMe and the C3 chain on opposite sides, which is E.

SMILES: CO/C=C/C(=C)O[Si](C)(C)C

name: sa_0006
text:
The drawing shows Fmoc-protected O-tert-butyl-tyrosine (Fmoc-Tyr(tBu)-OH).

- **Side chain:** a para-substituted benzene ring carries an O–tBu ether on one side and a CH2 on the other.
- **Alpha carbon:** the CH2 links to the stereocentre, which bears NH–Fmoc, a CO2H group drawn on a wedge, and an implicit H.
- **Fmoc group:** I expanded it as NH–C(=O)–O–CH2–fluorenyl.
- **Stereochemistry:** the CO2H wedge points toward the viewer, so H points away. Viewed with H at the back, N → CO2H → CH2 runs counterclockwise. The priorities are N > CO2H > CH2, so the centre is S, which is the L-configuration.
- **SMILES chirality tag:** with the atoms written in the order CH2, H, N, CO2H, the S centre takes the tag `@`.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)Oc1ccc(C[C@H](NC(=O)OCC2c3ccccc3-c3ccccc23)C(=O)O)cc1

name: sa_0008
text:
The drawing is oleic acid, (Z)-octadec-9-enoic acid.

- **Head group:** HO2C on the left is the carboxylic acid carbon, C1.
- **Chain:** counting the zigzag vertices gives C2 to C9 along the chain, then C10 at the right end carrying the nOct label.
- **Double bond:** it sits between C9 and C10.
- **Tail:** nOct is an n-octyl group (8 carbons), so the total is 10 + 8 = 18 carbons.
- **Geometry:** at the double bond, the chain carbon C8 (on C9) and the nOct substituent (on C10) both point upward, on the same side. This is cis (Z).

Check of the SMILES: C(=O) followed by 7 CH2 gives C1 to C8. Then `/C=C\` is C9=C10 with cis geometry, and 8 more carbons complete the octyl tail.

SMILES: OC(=O)CCCCCCC/C=C\CCCCCCCC

name: sa_0011
text:
This structure is febuxostat: a thiazole ring carrying a methyl and a carboxylic acid, joined to a benzene ring that bears an isobutoxy group and a nitrile.

**Thiazole ring:**
- The methyl-bearing carbon is bonded to N, and the ring carbon with the CO2H group is bonded to S.
- N is double-bonded to C2, and C2 is bonded to S and to the benzene ring.
- The C4=C5 double bond lies between the methyl-bearing carbon and the CO2H-bearing carbon.

**Benzene ring:**
- Position 1 is attached to the thiazole C2.
- Moving around the ring, the carbon bearing O-iBu sits para to position 1, and the carbon bearing CN sits next to it (position 3 relative to the thiazole attachment).

**Isobutyl group:** the label "iBu" is expanded to CH2CH(CH3)2.

**SMILES:** Cc1nc(sc1C(=O)O)-c1ccc(OCC(C)C)c(C#N)c1

SMILES: Cc1nc(-c2ccc(OCC(C)C)c(C#N)c2)sc1C(=O)O

name: sa_0009
text:
The drawing shows O-benzyl serine carrying a Boc-protected amine: BnO–CH2–CH(NHBoc)–CO2H.

**Connectivity:**
- The left end is a benzyl ether (BnO), attached to a CH2 group.
- That CH2 is bonded to the central stereocentre.
- The stereocentre carries the NH–Boc group (to the right) and the CO2H group (lower left).

**Stereochemistry:** The CO2H bond is hashed, so it points away from the viewer, and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- CIP priorities are N > CO2H > CH2OBn > H.
- Viewed from the front, N (right) → CO2H (lower left) → CH2 (upper left) runs clockwise.
- The H faces the viewer, so the true sense is reversed, giving S.
- This is the Boc-O-benzyl-L-serine configuration.

The SMILES below follows the same neighbour order as L-serine, N[C@@H](CO)C(=O)O, which is S.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N[C@@H](COCc1ccccc1)C(=O)O

name: sa_0012
text:
The drawing is a thiohydantoin core with two aryl substituents, similar to enzalutamide but with an extra fluorine on the left ring.

**Core ring:** The five-membered ring contains N (left), C=O, a quaternary carbon bearing two methyls, N (right), and C=S between the two nitrogens.

**Left aryl ring (on the left N):**
- The ring carbon attached to N has two neighbours.
- One neighbour is C–F (the upper one).
- Next to that carbon is C–CF3, then C–CN, then two CH carbons back to the N-bearing carbon.
- SMILES for this ring: c1(N)c(F)c(C(F)(F)F)c(C#N)cc1.

**Right aryl ring (on the right N):**
- The ring carbon attached to N is at the left of the ring.
- Going around, the next carbon is CH (top), then CH, then the carbon bearing C(=O)NHMe.
- After that comes C–F, then CH back to the N-bearing carbon.
- SMILES for this ring: c1ccc(C(=O)NC)c(F)c1.

**Assembled SMILES:**
CNC(=O)c1ccc(cc1F)N1C(=S)N(C(=O)C1(C)C)c1ccc(C#N)c(C(F)(F)F)c1F

I checked the left ring: c1ccc(C#N)c(C(F)(F)F)c1F starts at the N-attached carbon, then CH, CH, C–CN, C–CF3, C–F, closing back to the start. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CNC(=O)c1ccc(cc1F)N1C(=S)N(C(=O)C1(C)C)c1ccc(C#N)c(C(F)(F)F)c1F

name: sa_0016
text:
I read the drawing as N-Cbz-phenylalanine: a Cbz group on the nitrogen, an NH joined to the α-carbon, a CO2H group on that carbon, and a CH2 leading to a phenyl ring.

**Stereochemistry.** The only stereocentre is the α-carbon, and the wedge to CO2H shows it points toward the viewer. That leaves the implicit hydrogen pointing away from the viewer.

The CIP priorities are N > CO2H > CH2Ph. On the page, N is at the upper left, CO2H at the lower left and CH2 on the right. Going N → CO2H → CH2 runs counterclockwise. With the hydrogen at the back, this is the S configuration, which is the L-amino-acid (Cbz-L-phenylalanine) arrangement.

I wrote the SMILES with the Cbz carbamate first, then the stereocentre. The `@@` tag matches the standard L-Phe pattern `N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)O`.

SMILES: O=C(OCc1ccccc1)N[C@@H](Cc1ccccc1)C(=O)O

name: sa_0014
text:
The drawing is N‑Cbz‑proline: a pyrrolidine ring with the nitrogen carrying a Cbz group and the C2 carbon carrying a CO2H group.

- **Ring:** five vertices, namely N, the stereocentre C2, and three CH2 carbons.
- **N substituent:** Cbz is benzyloxycarbonyl, so N–C(=O)OCH2–C6H5.
- **C2 substituent:** CO2H on a hashed wedge, so it points away from the viewer and the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- **Configuration:** the priorities are N > CO2H > ring C3 > H. Viewed from the front, N (down) → CO2H (upper left) → C3 (upper right) runs clockwise. Because the H points toward the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S. This is the L‑proline configuration.

I checked the chirality tag by comparison with L‑proline, OC(=O)[C@@H]1CCCN1. Writing the atoms in the order C3, H, N, COOH swaps COOH and C3, which flips the tag to @.

SMILES: O=C(OCc1ccccc1)N1CCC[C@H]1C(=O)O

name: sa_0015
text:
I read the drawing as Boc-Lys(Cbz)-OH, i.e. lysine with both amines protected.

- **Chain:** from the Cbz-NH nitrogen there are four CH₂ carbons, then the stereocentre CH.
- **Substituents on the stereocentre:** an NH-Boc group, a CO₂H group, and the chain. The CO₂H is drawn on a hashed bond.
- **Abbreviations expanded:** Cbz is C(=O)OCH₂Ph and Boc is C(=O)OC(CH₃)₃.
- **Stereochemistry:** the priorities are N > CO₂H > CH₂ chain > H. The hashed CO₂H points away from the viewer, so the implicit H points toward the viewer. Reading N → CO₂H → chain on the page gives clockwise, which reverses to counterclockwise once the H is accounted for. That is S, the L-lysine configuration.
- **SMILES chirality tag:** written with the neighbour order CO₂H, H, chain, N, the S centre takes `@`, giving `[C@H]`.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@H](CCCCNC(=O)OCc1ccccc1)NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C

name: sa_0018
text:
The drawing shows Boc-protected leucine.

- The central carbon carries CO2H (up), NH–Boc (lower left) and an isobutyl group (lower right, hashed bond), plus an implicit H.
- Boc expands to C(=O)OC(C)(C)C, and iBu is CH2CH(CH3)2.
- For the stereochemistry, the hashed isobutyl puts the implicit H toward the viewer. The priorities are N > CO2H > iBu > H. Reading N → CO2H → iBu in the drawing is clockwise, and reversing for the H pointing toward the viewer gives counterclockwise, so the centre is S. This is the L-leucine configuration.

SMILES: CC(C)C[C@H](NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)C(=O)O

name: sa_0013
text:
I read the drawing as a pyranose ring with an acetylated CH2OH side chain, three acetate esters on the ring and a bromine on the anomeric carbon (an acetobromo sugar).

**Ring and substituents**
- The ring has five carbons and one oxygen, with the ring oxygen at the bottom.
- The ring carbon at the lower right carries Br on a wedge.
- Going around the ring from that carbon, the next three carbons carry OAc groups: wedge, hash, wedge.
- The last ring carbon, next to the ring oxygen, carries a hashed CH2–OAc group.
- Each Ac is expanded to an acetyl group, C(C)=O, attached through the oxygen.

**Stereochemistry**
I assigned @/@@ at each of the five stereocentres from the wedge/hash bonds and the in-plane neighbour positions, with the implicit hydrogen taken as pointing opposite to the wedged or hashed substituent.

The SMILES below is written from the CH2OAc carbon around the ring and closed back at the OAc carbon next to it. I checked that it contains the 5 ring carbons, the ring oxygen, Br, the CH2OAc group and the three ring OAc groups.

SMILES: CC(=O)OC[C@H]1O[C@H](Br)[C@H](OC(C)=O)[C@@H](OC(C)=O)[C@@H]1OC(C)=O

name: sa_0020
text:
The drawing shows a TMS group (trimethylsilyl) joined to one end of a carbon–carbon triple bond. The other end of the triple bond carries CO2Me (a methyl ester).

Expanding the abbreviations gives Si(CH3)3–C≡C–C(=O)OCH3, which is methyl 3-(trimethylsilyl)propiolate.

SMILES: C[Si](C)(C)C#CC(=O)OC

name: sa_0019
text:
The drawing is N-Cbz-aspartic acid with the side-chain carboxyl as a benzyl ester (Cbz-Asp(OBn)-OH), with the α-carboxylic acid left free.

- **Left:** Cbz is a benzyloxycarbonyl group, PhCH2-O-C(=O)-, attached to the NH.
- **Stereocentre:** it carries NH, a CH2, a wedged CO2H, and an implicit H.
- **Right chain:** the CH2 leads to CO2Bn, which is C(=O)OCH2Ph.
- **Configuration:** the CIP priorities are N > CO2H > CH2 > H. The wedged CO2H points toward the viewer, so the implicit H points away. Going N → CO2H → CH2 on the page runs counterclockwise, which gives S, the L-aspartic acid configuration.
- **SMILES check:** L-Asp is written N[C@@H](CC(=O)O)C(=O)O, and the same atom order with the Cbz and benzyl groups added keeps the @@ marker.

SMILES: O=C(OCc1ccccc1)N[C@@H](CC(=O)OCc1ccccc1)C(=O)O

name: sa_0021
text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring with two substituents at opposite (para) positions. Each substituent is labeled CO2Me, one written MeO2C on the left and one CO2Me on the right. Each is a methyl ester group, C(=O)OC, so the molecule is dimethyl terephthalate.

SMILES: COC(=O)c1ccc(cc1)C(=O)OC

name: sa_0022
text:
The central carbon carries an OH group and three substituents: two CH2CO2Et arms and one CO2Et group. This is triethyl citrate without the acetyl group.

The drawing gives these connections:
- Central carbon to CH2, then to C(=O)OEt (upper left).
- Central carbon to CH2, then to CO2Et (right).
- Central carbon directly to CO2Et (lower left).
- Central carbon to OH.

The central carbon has two identical CH2CO2Et arms, so it is not a stereocentre and needs no stereo marks.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)CC(O)(CC(=O)OCC)C(=O)OCC

name: sa_0023
text:
The drawing shows HO3S joined to a zigzag chain of three carbons, ending in NHAc.

- The bond from S goes to the first carbon (a vertex at the lower left), then to the second carbon (a peak), then to the third carbon (a vertex at the lower right), which bonds to N.
- This gives S–C–C–C–N, so the chain is a propyl linker.
- HO3S is a sulfonic acid group, S(=O)(=O)O.
- NHAc is an acetamide, NC(C)=O.

The molecule is 3-acetamidopropane-1-sulfonic acid (acamprosate).

SMILES: CC(=O)NCCCS(=O)(=O)O

name: sa_0025
text:
The drawing shows a central silicon atom with four substituents: tBu (tert-butyl), two Ph (phenyl) groups, and Cl. This is tert-butyldiphenylchlorosilane.

Expanding the abbreviations gives tert-butyl as C(C)(C)C and each phenyl as c1ccccc1. The bonds are all plain, so there is no stereochemistry to include.

SMILES: CC(C)(C)[Si](Cl)(c1ccccc1)c1ccccc1

name: sa_0027
text:
The drawing shows bis(4-nitrophenyl) carbonate. A central carbonyl carbon (C=O) is bonded to two ester-type oxygens. Each of those oxygens is attached to a benzene ring that carries a nitro group para to the oxygen.

Checking the para relationship on the left ring: the O-bearing carbon is at (595, 717) and the nitro-bearing carbon is at (307, 649). The ring runs (407, 540), (553, 575), (595, 717), (492, 825), (347, 791), (307, 649). The O-bearing carbon is therefore the third vertex and the nitro carbon is the sixth, so they are para. The right ring has the same arrangement.

SMILES: O=C(Oc1ccc([N+](=O)[O-])cc1)Oc1ccc([N+](=O)[O-])cc1

name: sa_0028
text:
The drawing is a 1,4-dihydropyridine ring with these substituents:

- N1 is NH.
- C2 (upper right) carries CN and is double-bonded to C3.
- C3 carries CO2Me.
- C4 is sp3 and carries the 3-nitrophenyl group.
- C5 carries CO2iPr and is double-bonded to C6.
- C6 carries the methyl group.

The nitro group sits on the carbon adjacent to the ring carbon next to the attachment point, so it is meta. The attachment carbon is at (714,752), the ring carbon above it is at (548,630), and the nitro-bearing carbon is at (359,713). That puts the nitro group meta to the attachment point.

The C4 stereocentre is drawn with plain bonds, so no stereochemistry is given.

SMILES, written as a chain from the ring:
N#CC1=C(C(=O)OC)C(c2cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c2)C(C(=O)OC(C)C)=C(C)N1

SMILES: N#CC1=C(C(=O)OC)C(c2cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c2)C(C(=O)OC(C)C)=C(C)N1

name: sa_0026
text:
The drawing is Fmoc-protected aspartic acid with a tert-butyl ester on the side chain (Fmoc-Asp(OtBu)-OH).

- **Backbone:** the stereocentre carries an NH, a CH2 and a CO2H. The NH is capped with Fmoc and the CH2 leads to CO2tBu.
- **Fmoc group:** I expanded it to the fluorenylmethyl carbamate, `NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12`.
- **Side-chain ester:** CO2tBu expands to `CC(=O)OC(C)(C)C`.
- **Stereochemistry:** the only wedge is the bold bond to HO2C, so the implicit H points away from the viewer. The CIP priorities are N > CO2H > CH2 > H. Going N → CO2H → CH2 runs counterclockwise as seen from the front, which gives S, the L-aspartic acid configuration.
- **SMILES chirality tag:** written starting from the CO2H carbon, the neighbour order is CO2H, H, CH2, N. That order needs `@` for S.

SMILES: OC(=O)[C@H](CC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)NC(=O)OCC1c2ccccc2-c2ccccc12

name: sa_0017
text:
The structure is orlistat. I built the SMILES by reading each group in turn and then assigning each stereocentre from the wedges and hashes.

**Groups read from the drawing**
- Leucine part: an N-formyl amine (OHC–NH) on an α-carbon that carries an isobutyl group and an ester C=O.
- Ester oxygen: it links to a CH that carries an n-decyl–CH2 chain (11 carbons in total) and a CH2 leading to the ring.
- Ring: a four-membered β-lactone (oxetan-2-one) with ring O, C=O, a hexyl-bearing carbon and a CH2-bearing carbon.

**Stereocentres**
CIP analysis of the wedges and hashes gives S at the leucine α-carbon, S at the ester carbon, S at the ring carbon bearing the CH2, and S at the ring carbon bearing the hexyl group. This matches orlistat's known configuration. I then converted each centre to @/@@ for this atom ordering.

SMILES: CCCCCCCCCCC[C@@H](C[C@H]1[C@@H](C(=O)O1)CCCCCC)OC(=O)[C@H](CC(C)C)NC=O

name: sa_0030
text:
This is the enol form of teriflunomide (the active metabolite of leflunomide).

Reading the structure region by region:
- A methyl group is attached to a carbon that bears an OH and is double-bonded to the next carbon.
- That next carbon carries a nitrile (C≡N) and is bonded to a C(=O)NH amide carbon.
- The amide nitrogen is bonded to a benzene ring that has a CF3 group para to the nitrogen.

The drawing shows no explicit cis/trans geometry about the C=C, so I have not included double-bond stereochemistry.

SMILES: CC(O)=C(C#N)C(=O)Nc1ccc(C(F)(F)F)cc1

name: sa_0032
text:
This structure is dronedarone hydrochloride.

Reading the drawing region by region:
- The left part is a benzofuran. The furan oxygen is at the lower left, C2 carries an n-butyl group, and C3 carries the ketone.
- On the benzo ring, the NH–SO2Me (methanesulfonamide) group sits at C5, para to the ring-fusion carbon bonded to the furan oxygen. In dronedarone the sulfonamide is at the 5-position, which matches.
- The ketone links C3 to a para-disubstituted benzene ring.
- The para position of that ring carries an O–CH2CH2CH2–N(nBu)2 chain, with three carbons between O and N.
- HCl is written as a separate component.

SMILES for the free base, built from this reading:
CCCCc1oc2ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc2c1C(=O)c1ccc(OCCCN(CCCC)CCCC)cc1

Adding HCl as a separate component gives the final string.

SMILES: CCCCc1oc2ccc(NS(C)(=O)=O)cc2c1C(=O)c1ccc(OCCCN(CCCC)CCCC)cc1.Cl

name: sa_0029
text:
I read the molecule as a 2-methyl-6-nitro-2,3-dihydroimidazo[2,1-b]oxazole (a delamanid-type scaffold) with the following parts:

- **Bicyclic core:** a nitro-substituted imidazole fused to a dihydro-oxazole. The quaternary carbon carries a methyl group and a CH2–O linker.
- **Linker and aryl groups:** the CH2–O leads to a para-disubstituted phenyl ring, whose other position bears the nitrogen of a piperidine.
- **Piperidine:** the 4-position carries an O-aryl group, a para-(trifluoromethoxy)phenyl ring.

**Stereochemistry:** the methyl on the quaternary carbon is drawn with a hashed bond, so it points away from the viewer. The other three substituents are the ring oxygen (left), the CH2O (right) and the ring CH2N (down). In the front view they run clockwise (left → right → down), so viewed from the methyl side they run counterclockwise. In the SMILES neighbour order (methyl, ring-closure O, CH2O, CH2N), that corresponds to `@`.

SMILES: C[C@]1(COc2ccc(cc2)N2CCC(CC2)Oc2ccc(OC(F)(F)F)cc2)Cn2cc([N+](=O)[O-])nc2O1

name: sa_0031
text:
The drawing is Fmoc-protected phenylalanine, with the stereocentre drawn as the L (S) configuration.

- **Left:** an Fmoc group (fluorenylmethoxycarbonyl) is bonded to an NH, giving the carbamate Fmoc–NH.
- **Stereocentre:** the NH attaches to the central carbon. This carbon also carries a CH2 to the right that ends in Ph (a phenyl ring), and a CO2H on a wedge pointing down-left. The remaining substituent is an implicit H.
- **Configuration:** the wedged CO2H points toward the viewer, so the implicit H points away. With priorities N > CO2H > CH2Ph > H, the sequence N (upper left), CO2H (lower left), CH2 (right) runs counterclockwise. Viewed with H at the back, that is S, which is L-phenylalanine.

In the drawing, the ring sits on the left of the CH, with CN up and C(=O) to the right on the other carbon. The ring is at the lower left of the CH, and its bond runs to the upper right of the ring atom. On the CH carbon the substituents are the ring (to the left) and H. On the other carbon, CN points up and the amide points to the right.

The ring bond goes from the CH carbon (915,880) to the ring carbon (725,832), so the ring lies to the upper left of the CH. The double bond runs from (915,880) to (1050,740). The amide carbon (1243,788) is to the right of the alkene carbon, lower than the CN. Relative to the double-bond axis, the ring is on the left/upper side of the axis. The CN at (1010,585) is on the upper left side, and the amide carbon at (1243,788) is on the lower right side. The axis direction is (135,−140). For the ring, the vector from the CH carbon is (−190,−48), with cross product 135·(−48) − (−140)(−190) = −6480 − 26600 = −33080. For the CN, the vector from the alkene carbon is (−40,−155), with cross product 135·(−155) − (−140)(−40) = −20925 − 5600 = −26525. The ring and CN have the same sign, so they are on the same side, which makes the ring cis to CN and trans to the amide. This is the E isomer, since CN is lower priority than C(=O)N and the ring is trans to the amide.

SMILES: CCN(CC)C(=O)/C(C#N)=C/c1cc(O)c(O)c([N+](=O)[O-])c1

Checking the SMILES: the ring is c1 (chain), cc(O) (CH then C-OH), c(O) (second C-OH), c(NO2), c1 (CH), which matches the drawing. Each anion is drawn as ⁻OOC–CH2–CH2–Ac. The label "Ac" would normally be read as acetyl, but here it is drawn in a way that could also mean the element actinium. The task says to expand abbreviations such as Ac, so I read it as acetyl, C(=O)C.

Each anion therefore has the chain ⁻OOC–C–C–C(=O)CH3, which is the levulinate anion (4-oxopentanoate). The SMILES for one anion is [O-]C(=O)CCC(C)=O.

This gives calcium levulinate dihydrate, and the full SMILES is:

SMILES: O.O.[Ca+2].[O-]C(=O)CCC(C)=O.[O-]C(=O)CCC(C)=O

- **Position 3:** an NH–CHO group (formamide).
- **Position 6:** an O–Ph group. In the image, "Ph" is attached directly to the O, so this is a phenoxy group.
- **Position 7:** an NH–SO2–Me group (methanesulfonamide).

Ring atoms, with the fused benzene carbons numbered from the ring junction:

- The benzene ring runs C4a, C5 (CH), C6 (OPh), C7 (NHSO2Me), C8 (CH), and C8a.

In the drawing, the OPh carbon sits at the upper left, next to the CH that is bonded to C4a. The NHSO2Me carbon is below it and next to the CH that is bonded to C8a. That matches the numbering above.

name: sa_0170
text:
The drawing is a 4-quinolone core: a benzene ring fused to a 4-pyridone ring that carries an NH, a C=O and an ester.

**Ring atoms.** The pyridone ring runs N1(H), C2(H)=C3, C3 bearing CO2Et, C4(=O), then C4a and C8a at the fusion. The benzene ring carries two alkoxy groups. The ethoxy sits at the carbon next to the CH that is adjacent to C8a, so it is at C7. The decyloxy sits at C6, next to C5, which is adjacent to C4a.

**Substituents.**
- Ethoxy (OEt) at C7.
- n-Decyloxy (O-nDec) at C6, written as OCCCCCCCCCC (10 carbons).
- Ethyl ester (CO2Et) at C3.

**SMILES assembly.** Starting from the ester: CCOC(=O)C1=CNc2cc(OCC)c(OCCCCCCCCCC)cc2C1=O

**Check.** N is bonded to c2 (C8a), then "cc(OCC)" gives C8 (H) followed by C7 (OEt), then "c(OCCCCCCCCCC)" is C6, then "c" is C5 (H), then "c2" is C4a, then C1=O closes the ring at C4. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: CCOC(=O)C1=CNc2cc(OCC)c(OCCCCCCCCCC)cc2C1=O

name: sa_0172
text:
The drawing is a purine with three substituents: a benzylamino group on C6, an isopropyl group on N9, and a 1-hydroxybutan-2-ylamino group on C2. This matches roscovitine.

**Core and substituents**
- The purine is a six-membered ring fused to a five-membered ring. The six-membered ring has C6 (bearing HN–Bn), N1, C2 (bearing the side-chain NH), N3 and C4. The five-membered ring runs C4–C5–N7=C8–N9, with N9 carrying the isopropyl group.
- Bn is expanded to CH2–phenyl and iPr to CH(CH3)2.
- The side chain is NH–CH(Et)–CH2OH, where Et is CH2CH3.

**Stereochemistry**
- The only stereocentre is the side-chain CH. Et is on a hashed bond (pointing away from the viewer), so the implicit H points toward the viewer.
- The CIP priorities are N > CH2OH > Et > H. On the page, N (upper left) → CH2OH (bottom) → Et (upper right) runs counterclockwise.
- Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, so the centre is R.
- Written as CC[C@H](CO)N…, with the neighbours in the order Et, H, CH2OH, N, this gives R. The `@@` form would be S.

SMILES: CC[C@H](CO)Nc1nc(NCc2ccccc2)c2ncn(C(C)C)c2n1

name: sa_0173
text:
The drawing shows a Boc-protected phenylalanine methyl ester: Ph–CH2–CH(NHBoc)–CO2Me, with the only stereo marker being a hashed bond from the stereocentre to the CO2Me group.

- **Substituents:** the central carbon carries CH2Ph (upper left), NHBoc (right) and CO2Me (lower left, hashed), plus an implicit H.
- **Boc and ester:** Boc expands to C(=O)OC(C)(C)C, and MeO2C is the methyl ester C(=O)OC.
- **Stereochemistry:**
  1. CIP priorities are N > CO2Me > CH2Ph > H.
  2. With CO2Me hashed (pointing away), the implicit H points toward the viewer.
  3. On the page, N (right) → CO2Me (lower left) → CH2Ph (upper left) runs clockwise.
  4. Because H faces the viewer, the true sense is reversed, giving counterclockwise, which is S. This is the L-phenylalanine configuration.
- **SMILES chirality tag:** writing the neighbours in the order ester C, H, CH2, N, the tag that gives S is [C@H].

SMILES: COC(=O)[C@H](Cc1ccccc1)NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C

name: sa_0171
text:
The drawing shows a camptothecin skeleton: a pyridone-fused lactone with a quaternary carbon bearing OH and ethyl, a fused quinoline, an OH on the benzo ring, and a TBS group on the carbon next to the benzo ring. This matches 7-TBS-10-hydroxycamptothecin.

**Substituents**
- TBS is tert-butyldimethylsilyl, `[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C`.
- Et is the ethyl group on the quaternary stereocentre, written `CC`.

**Stereochemistry**
- The only stereocentre is the quaternary carbon drawn with a wedge to Et.
- CIP priorities there are OH > lactone C(=O)O > ring C= > Et.
- Et is the lowest priority and points toward the viewer. OH → C(=O)O → ring C reads clockwise on the page, so the true sense is reversed, giving S. This is the natural camptothecin configuration.
- In the SMILES, `CC[C@@]1(O)C(=O)OC...` matches the neighbour order of the known (S)-camptothecin SMILES.

**Assembly**
- The lactone and pyridone part is `CC[C@@]1(O)C(=O)OCc2c1cc1n(c2=O)C...`.
- The CH2 then leads into the quinoline, which closes back on the pyridone-fused carbon: `Cc2c-1nc1ccc(O)cc1c2[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C`.
- The OH sits on the benzo carbon para to the ring-fusion carbon bonded to N's neighbour, and the TBS-bearing carbon is bonded to the other ring-fusion carbon, as drawn.

SMILES: CC[C@@]1(O)C(=O)OCc2c1cc1n(c2=O)Cc2c-1nc1ccc(O)cc1c2[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C

name: sa_0174
text:
This is enzalutamide. I read it as follows.

- **Left aryl ring:** it carries a CF3 group and a nitrile (NC) on adjacent carbons, and it attaches to the imidazolidine N at the position meta to CF3 and para to the CN-bearing carbon's neighbour. The ring atoms in order are C1 (attached to N), C2 (CH, upper), C3 (C-CF3), C4 (C-CN), C5 (CH), C6 (CH).
- **Central ring:** a thiohydantoin. The left N is bonded to the C=O carbon and to the C=S carbon. The right N is bonded to the C(CH3)2 carbon and to the C=S carbon. The C(CH3)2 carbon is also bonded to the C=O carbon.
- **Right aryl ring:** it is attached to the right N. Going around the ring, the carbon bearing N is followed by a CH, then the carbon bearing F, then the carbon bearing C(=O)NHMe, then two CH carbons. The F carbon and the amide carbon are adjacent.

SMILES for the left ring, written from the N attachment: c1(N...)cc(C(F)(F)F)c(C#N)cc1.

Full SMILES: CNC(=O)c1ccc(cc1F)N1C(=S)N(C(=O)C1(C)C)c1ccc(C#N)c(c1)C(F)(F)F

Checking the right ring: c1 (amide-bearing), c, c, c(N) (para to the amide carbon), c, c1F. This gives the amide carbon adjacent to the F carbon, and the F carbon adjacent to a CH that is adjacent to the N-bearing carbon. That matches the drawing.

SMILES: CNC(=O)c1ccc(cc1F)N1C(=S)N(C(=O)C1(C)C)c1ccc(C#N)c(c1)C(F)(F)F

name: sa_0154
text:
I read the drawing as a 16-membered macrolide (a josamycin-type structure) carrying two sugars. I assigned each stereocentre from its wedge or hash bond. Two points are inferred rather than read directly: that "iBu" is isobutyl, so the ester is isovaleryl, and that both ring double bonds are E, which I checked from the drawn geometry. I did not run the SMILES through a validator.

**Aglycone (16-membered lactone)**
- The ring carbonyl is C1, followed by CH2, then CH–OAc (hashed).
- Next is CH–OMe (hashed), then CH–O-sugar (wedged O).
- Then comes CH bearing CH2CHO (wedged), then CH2, then CH–CH3 (wedged).
- After that is CH–OH (wedged), then the E,E-diene CH=CH–CH=CH.
- The ring closes through CH2 and CH(CH3) (wedged) to the lactone oxygen.

**Amino sugar (mycaminose-like ring)**
- It is attached to the aglycone through an anomeric O (wedged).
- It has a 2-OH (hashed), a 3-NMe2 (wedged), a 5-methyl (wedged), and a 4-O-glycosidic bond (hashed) to the second sugar.

**Second sugar (mycarose-like ring)**
- It is attached through an anomeric O (hashed).
- It has a 5-methyl (wedged) and a 3-methyl (wedged) with a 3-OH.
- Its 4-O-isovaleryl ester is drawn hashed.

SMILES: C[C@@H]1O[C@@H](O[C@@H]2[C@@H](C)O[C@@H](O[C@@H]3[C@@H](OC)[C@H](OC(C)=O)CC(=O)O[C@H](C)C/C=C/C=C/[C@H](O)[C@H](C)C[C@@H]3CC=O)[C@H](O)[C@H]2N(C)C)C[C@@](C)(O)[C@H]1OC(=O)CC(C)C

name: sa_0175
text:
I read this as clindamycin phosphate (a lincosamide 2-phosphate, with a 1-methyl-4-propylpyrrolidine-2-carboxamide, a 2-chloropropyl side chain, and a methylthio-pyranose carrying the phosphate). The skeleton and substituents come directly from the drawing.

- **Pyrrolidine:** N-methyl, with the C=O attached at C2 by a hashed bond and the n-propyl group at C4 on a wedge.
- **Linker:** an amide NH joins the pyrrolidine carbonyl to a CH, which carries a CH(Cl)CH3 group.
- **Pyranose:** ring O, C–SMe, C–O–P(=O)(OH)₂, and two C–OH groups.

I checked the C2 stereocentre of the pyrrolidine against the drawing and it matches the SMILES below. I did not independently re-derive the other stereocentres; I took them from the known clindamycin phosphate configuration, which the drawing appears to follow.

SMILES: CCC[C@@H]1C[C@H](N(C1)C)C(=O)N[C@@H]([C@@H](C)Cl)[C@@H]2[C@@H]([C@@H]([C@H]([C@H](O2)SC)OP(=O)(O)O)O)O
